title: CBSE Class 10 | AI | Communication skill | Revisiting Ai project cycle & Ethics Frameworks for AI
description: CBSE Class 10 | AI | Communication skill | Revisiting Ai project cycle & Ethics Frameworks for AI
chapters: Revisiting Ai project cycle & Ethics Frameworks for AI
subject: ai-artificial-intelligence

questions.question: The word 'Communication' is derived from the Latin word 'communis', which means:
questions.explanation: The root word 'communis' implies establishing a common ground of understanding between the sender and receiver.
questions.hint: Think about what happens when two people exchange ideas.

questions.question: In the communication cycle, what is the process of converting an idea into a message by the sender called?
questions.explanation: Encoding is the step where the sender translates their thoughts into words, symbols, or gestures to form a message.
questions.hint: It involves "packaging" the information before sending it.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the 7Cs of effective communication?
questions.explanation: The 7Cs are Clear, Concise, Concrete, Correct, Coherent, Complete, and Courteous. "Colorful" is not part of this professional framework.
questions.hint: Look for the option that relates more to art than to professional message delivery.

questions.question: Using exact facts, figures, and specific details in your communication refers to which of the 7Cs?
questions.explanation: Concrete communication is specific, definitive, and vivid rather than vague and general. It relies on facts and data.
questions.hint: Think of a building material that is solid and hard.

questions.question: When a receiver interprets the message and understands the sender's intent, this process is known as:
questions.explanation: Decoding is the mental process where the receiver breaks down the message to comprehend its meaning.
questions.hint: It is the opposite of encoding.

questions.question: Which element of the communication cycle confirms that the message has been successfully received and understood?
questions.explanation: Feedback is the receiver's response, which allows the sender to know if the communication was effective.
questions.hint: It completes the communication loop.

questions.question: Pointing a finger at someone while speaking is an example of:
questions.explanation: Gestures, facial expressions, and body language fall under non-verbal communication.
questions.hint: It involves actions rather than words.

questions.question: What percentage of communication is often attributed to body language, according to common communication theories (like the Mehrabian rule)?
questions.explanation: Research suggests that up to 55% of the impact of face-to-face communication comes from body language and visual cues.
questions.hint: It constitutes the clear majority of face-to-face impact.

questions.question: A presentation relying heavily on graphs, charts, and diagrams primarily utilizes which method of communication?
questions.explanation: Visual communication uses visual aids like graphs, images, and charts to convey information quickly and clearly.
questions.hint: It requires the sense of sight to interpret the primary message.

questions.question: Which of the following is a physical barrier to effective communication?
questions.explanation: Physical barriers relate to environmental factors, such as noise, distance, or faulty equipment, that block the message.
questions.hint: It is an external disruption you can hear or see.

questions.question: A person misunderstanding a message because they do not know the technical jargon used is experiencing a:
questions.explanation: Linguistic barriers occur when there are differences in language, vocabulary, or jargon that prevent understanding.
questions.hint: This barrier relates directly to words and language.

questions.question: The ability to manage one's own emotions and read the emotions of others to avoid conflicts refers to overcoming which barrier?
questions.explanation: Interpersonal barriers stem from personal feelings, attitudes, or emotional states that hinder objective communication.
questions.hint: It happens directly between two people's personalities.

questions.question: According to the rules of basic writing skills, a complete sentence must contain at least:
questions.explanation: A basic complete sentence requires a subject (who or what the sentence is about) and a verb (the action or state).
questions.hint: Think "Who did what?"

questions.question: In the sentence "The quick brown fox jumps," what part of speech is "quick"?
questions.explanation: "Quick" modifies the noun "fox," describing a quality of the noun, which makes it an adjective.
questions.hint: It describes a noun.

questions.question: Which of the following is a Definite Article?
questions.explanation: "The" is the definite article used to point out a specific person, place, or thing. "A" and "An" are indefinite.
questions.hint: Used when talking about a specific, known noun.

questions.question: Which part of speech connects words, phrases, or clauses in a sentence (e.g., and, but, because)?
questions.explanation: Conjunctions serve as the "glue" in sentences to connect different parts together.
questions.hint: "Conjunction junction, what's your function?" (Linking words).

questions.question: Keeping a message logically connected so that the points flow smoothly into one another satisfies which 'C' of communication?
questions.explanation: Coherence ensures that all parts of the message are logically linked and make sense as a whole.
questions.hint: It means everything sticks together logically.

questions.question: If a sender uses grammatically accurate sentences and appropriate vocabulary, they are practicing which 'C'?
questions.explanation: Correctness in communication means using proper grammar, spelling, and factual accuracy.
questions.hint: It means making no errors.

questions.question: "Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any questions." This sentence best demonstrates which communication principle?
questions.explanation: Courteous communication is polite, respectful, and shows consideration for the receiver.
questions.hint: It shows good manners.

questions.question: A well-structured paragraph should ideally begin with a:
questions.explanation: The topic sentence introduces the main idea of the paragraph, guiding the reader on what to expect.
questions.hint: It summarizes the paragraph's main point right away.

questions.question: Slouching in a chair during a job interview sends a negative non-verbal message regarding your:
questions.explanation: Posture is a key element of body language that conveys your level of interest, confidence, and professionalism.
questions.hint: It relates to how you hold your body.

questions.question: Overcoming linguistic barriers can be effectively achieved by:

options.text: Using simple, clear language and avoiding jargon
Sending a written letter instead of talking

questions.explanation: Simplifying language ensures that vocabulary differences do not obstruct the core message.
questions.hint: Keep it simple.

questions.question: Which of the following best defines "Feedback" in the communication cycle?

options.text: The channel used to send the message
The receiver's response or reaction to the sender's message
The background noise during a conversation
The process of translating thoughts into words

questions.explanation: Feedback is the final step in the cycle where the receiver indicates their understanding of the message.
questions.hint: It is the "reply" to the original message.

questions.question: Written communication is generally preferred over verbal communication when:

options.text: A permanent record of the information is needed
The sender and receiver are in the same room

questions.explanation: Written communication provides a document trail, making it ideal for official policies, contracts, or complex instructions.
questions.hint: You can file it away for future reference.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of breaking text into paragraphs?

options.text: To make the document look longer
To group related sentences around a single main idea

questions.explanation: Paragraphs organize text into readable chunks, each focusing on a distinct concept or idea.
questions.hint: It organizes ideas into logical blocks.

questions.question: What is the correct sequential order of the first three stages in the AI Project Cycle?

options.text: Data Acquisition -> Problem Scoping -> Data Exploration
Problem Scoping -> Data Acquisition -> Data Exploration

questions.explanation: The cycle begins with defining the problem (Scoping), gathering data (Acquisition), and then analyzing that data (Exploration).
questions.hint: You must know the problem before you can collect data for it.

questions.question: In the Problem Scoping stage, the '4Ws Problem Canvas' is used. Which of the following is NOT one of the 4Ws?
questions.explanation: The 4Ws Canvas consists of Who (stakeholders), What (the problem), Where (context/location), and Why (the solution's value). "When" is not included.
questions.hint: Think about stakeholders, the issue, the context, and the reason, rather than the time.

questions.question: In the 4Ws canvas, the "Who" block helps us identify:

options.text: The stakeholders who are facing the problem
The environment where the problem occurs

questions.explanation: The "Who" block is dedicated to understanding the people or entities directly affected by the problem.
questions.hint: It refers to people or organizations.

questions.question: Which stage of the AI Project Cycle involves creating visual representations of the collected data to find trends and patterns?
questions.explanation: Data Exploration involves analyzing the data visually (graphs, charts) to understand its structure before building a model.
questions.hint: You are "looking around" the data to see what it contains.

questions.question: Acquiring data from sensors, web scraping, or public datasets takes place in which stage?
questions.explanation: Data Acquisition is the exact step where data necessary to solve the scoped problem is gathered from various sources.
questions.hint: "Acquisition" literally means to obtain or get something.

questions.question: An AI model that operates purely on explicit instructions and logical conditions set by a human developer is using a:
questions.explanation: Rule-based systems (like decision trees without ML) follow strict "If-Then" rules programmed by humans, unlike learning-based systems that find their own patterns.
questions.hint: The developer writes the "laws" the system must follow.

questions.question: If an AI system is trained on historical data so it can discover patterns and make predictions on its own, it is using a:
questions.explanation: Learning-based models (Machine Learning) use algorithms to learn from data patterns without being explicitly programmed for every scenario.
questions.hint: The machine teaches itself from past experiences.

questions.question: Which AI domain focuses on enabling machines to understand, interpret, and generate human language?
questions.explanation: NLP deals with text and speech, allowing AI to interact with humans via natural language (e.g., Chatbots, voice assistants).
questions.hint: It involves words, grammar, and speech.

questions.question: A facial recognition attendance system in a school is a prime application of which AI domain?
questions.explanation: Computer Vision enables AI to derive meaningful information from digital images, videos, and visual inputs, such as faces.
questions.hint: It gives the AI the ability to "see".

questions.question: The AI domain that heavily relies on statistics, numbers, and analyzing large datasets to predict future trends (like stock market prediction) is:
questions.explanation: Data Science focuses on analyzing numeric and categorical data to find correlations and make statistical predictions.
questions.hint: It deals heavily with spreadsheets and numbers.

questions.question: After an AI model is created, it must be tested using a specific set of data to check its accuracy before deployment. This stage is called:
questions.explanation: Evaluation is the final step in the cycle where the model's performance is tested against new, unseen data to ensure it works correctly.
questions.hint: It is like an exam for the AI.

questions.question: If a recruitment AI favors resumes with male names over female names because its historical training data had more men, this is an example of:
questions.explanation: Algorithmic bias occurs when an AI system reflects human biases present in its training data, leading to unfair outcomes.
questions.hint: It is a form of digital prejudice.

questions.question: Which ethical concern arises when AI systems continuously track a user's search history and location without explicit, clear consent?
questions.explanation: Collecting and storing personal user data without proper consent or security violates data privacy principles.
questions.hint: It involves your personal, secret information.

questions.question: The ethical principle that requires AI developers to be able to explain *how* an AI model makes its decisions is called:
questions.explanation: Transparency ensures that AI systems are not "black boxes" and that humans can understand the logic behind an AI's output.
questions.hint: It means seeing clearly through the process.

questions.question: If a self-driving car gets into an accident, deciding who is responsible (the driver, the manufacturer, or the AI developer) highlights the ethical issue of:
questions.explanation: Accountability in AI ethics deals with assigning responsibility for the actions and consequences of an autonomous system.
questions.hint: Who takes the blame?

questions.question: What does the "Why" block in the 4Ws Problem Canvas determine?

options.text: The benefits and value of solving the problem
The type of AI domain to use

questions.explanation: The "Why" block focuses on the solution's impact-why the problem is worth solving and how it benefits the stakeholders.
questions.hint: It looks for the core reason or motivation for the project.

questions.question: "Bioethics" in the context of AI primarily deals with:

options.text: The ethical implications of using AI in healthcare, biology, and human life

questions.explanation: Bioethics focuses on the intersection of technology and biology, ensuring AI respects human life, medical privacy, and genetic data rights.
questions.hint: "Bio" refers to life and medicine.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an AI acting as an "Intelligent Virtual Assistant" using NLP?
questions.explanation: Alexa and Siri process spoken human language (NLP) to perform tasks and generate human-like responses.
questions.hint: You talk to them on your phone or smart speaker.

questions.question: When dealing with AI Issues and Concerns, the fear that AI robots and software will replace human jobs is known as:
questions.explanation: Technological unemployment is the loss of jobs caused by technological change, a major societal concern regarding AI automation.
questions.hint: It relates to humans losing their livelihoods to machines.

questions.question: In the Data Exploration phase, which tool is a data scientist most likely to use?
questions.explanation: Visual tools like graphs and charts help analysts quickly spot outliers, trends, and patterns during exploration.
questions.hint: They are visual representations of numbers.

questions.question: Training Data and Testing Data are concepts primarily used during which stages?
questions.explanation: You use Training data to build the model (Modelling) and Testing data to check its accuracy (Evaluation).
questions.hint: One is for learning, the other is for the exam.

questions.question: In which AI Domain would you categorize an application that detects fake news by analyzing the sentiment and vocabulary of news articles?
questions.explanation: Analyzing text, vocabulary, and sentiment requires understanding language, which falls squarely under NLP.
questions.hint: It involves reading and understanding text.

questions.question: The phrase "Garbage In, Garbage Out" in AI implies that:

options.text: AI systems produce a lot of electronic waste
If the training data is poor or biased, the AI's output will also be poor or biased
AI is not useful for data science

questions.explanation: An AI model is only as good as the data it is trained on. Flawed data leads to flawed models.
questions.hint: Bad ingredients make a bad cake.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of an "Ethical Framework" in AI?

options.text: To make AI run faster on computers
To establish guidelines ensuring AI is developed safely, fairly, and responsibly
To prevent anyone from building AI

questions.explanation: Ethical frameworks are sets of guidelines and principles designed to steer AI development toward beneficial and harmless outcomes.
questions.hint: It acts as a moral compass for developers.

questions.question: The "What" block of the 4Ws canvas is used to:

options.text: Detail the exact nature of the problem being faced
List the names of the developers
Explain the programming language being used
Identify the server where data is stored

questions.explanation: The "What" block clearly defines the problem statement, what the issue is, and how it manifests.
questions.hint: It defines the core issue itself.
